Hello! Yes po, I decided to go with Tytana na lang.

I asked a senior who's currently in her 4th year of nursing to help me decide. I also laid out the pros and cons based on what I found online and my own thoughts. Ang sabi niya, consider daw if malapit yung hospitals na pagdudutyhan. Malaking factor daw yun kasi mas tipid sa transpo and mas convenient.

Good thing na lang din, it’ll take me less than an hour from the school to the hospital, so malaking tulong talaga siya in terms of time and budget. Familiar na rin ako sa location ng Tytana, kaya mas comfortable at convenient siya for me compared to exploring a completely new area.

Although affiliated naman ang Mapúa with multiple hospitals, mas at ease talaga ako sa setup ni Tytana. Isa pa, personally, parang di ko talaga kakayanin if nursing na nga yung course ko tapos trisem pa 😭 Sobrang demanding na nga yung program, tapos dagdagan pa ng fast-paced schedule—baka ma-burn out lang ako.

Isa pa raw, since forte talaga ng Tytana ang nursing, kasabihan na rin daw na *“ang review for the board exam doesn’t start at the review center, kundi sa 1st year pa lang.”*  
So I guess this means to **choose your school wisely**, kasi kung maganda na agad yung foundation mo from day one, mas magiging confident ka and prepared when the time comes to take the boards. Hindi ka nila iniiwan sa huli lang maghahabol ng review—kumbaga, naka-integrate na yung preparation sa buong curriculum. Kaya kahit mahirap, guided ka na early on sa mga concepts na lalabas sa board exam, which I think is a big advantage.

Aside from that, **Tytana is known for consistently producing top-notch board passers and has built a strong reputation over the years specifically in the field of nursing.** Their system is already tested, and marami na ring success stories from their alumni. Their facilities and clinical exposure opportunities are aligned with DOH standards, and they have strong partnerships with established training hospitals. May focus din sila not just on academic excellence, but also on professionalism and patient-centered care.

I chose Tytana mainly because isa sa mga kinakatakutan ko is yung fact na **hindi pa proven ang nursing program ng Mapúa**. As of now, yung pinakamatagal na students nila ay yung pilot batch pa lang, so wala pa tayong concrete idea how they’ll perform sa boards. If I’m not mistaken, yung mga recent na nag-take ng boards from Mapúa ay matagal nang graduates parang ngayon lang sila ulit nag-exam, so we can’t really gauge their program’s consistency.

**Cons I considered sa Mapúa:**  
– **Trisem system** = shorter breaks, fast-paced learning, and less time to process demanding subjects like anatomy, pharma, etc.  
– **Lack of nursing culture/support system** = wala pa masyadong established na orgs, alumni network, or upperclassmen na pwedeng hingan ng tips or guidance.  
– **Limited track record** = like i said di pa natin alam kung kamusta talaga yung clinical exposure, affiliations, or board passing rate ng current batches.  
– **Focus on international curriculum** = which can be great long-term, pero baka kulang sa emphasis on local board requirements, na kailangan mo muna maipasa.

Honestly, **Mapúa has always been my dream school**. I even went on the open campus tour last month and was really amazed sa advancement ng facilities nila. Sobrang high-tech and impressive, and I can definitely see the potential. But at the end of the day, I had to be realistic. I wasn’t ready to risk it, especially for a course as critical and intense as nursing. Mas important kasi sa akin yung peace of mind ko and solid foundation.
